title: Linked List Cycle
kidExplanation: Do the arrows ever loop? A slow turtle and a fast rabbit will meet if there is a cycle.
plainProblem: Linked List Cycle: Do the arrows ever loop? Worked example — input: head = [3,2,0,-4], pos = 1; expected output: true. Why: Cycle. Interview pattern to name out loud: Pointer rewriting on a linked list.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: To detect a cycle in a linked list, we can use the Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm. We maintain two pointers, 'slow' and 'fast', where 'slow' moves one step at a time and 'fast' moves two steps at a time. If there is a cycle in the linked list, the two pointers will eventually meet at some point. If there is no cycle, the 'fast' pointer will reach the end of the list.

# Linked List Cycle
# Idea: To detect a cycle in a linked list, we can use the Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm. We maintain two pointers, 'slow' and 'fast', where 'slow' moves one step at a time and 'fast' moves two steps at a time. If there is…
# Line comments below keep the same logic as the NeetCode 150 repo solution.

# Definition for singly-linked list.
# class ListNode:
#     def __init__(self, x):
#         self.val = x
#         self.next = None


class Solution:
    def hasCycle(self, head: ListNode) -> bool:
        if not head or not head.next:
            return False

        slow = head
        fast = head.next

        while slow != fast:
            if not fast or not fast.next:
                return False
            slow = slow.next
            fast = fast.next.next

        return True
